newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds declined sharply on Wednesday, amid a general sell-off in all major bond markets triggered by earlier German third quarter GDP data, which was at the high end of the forecasts.
"A consolidation was long overdue," a dealer in Madrid said. "But we are still positive as we are expecting a rate cut on December 13 and good news on the stability pact."

The December long term bond future lost 58 basis points to close at 112.07, after it had reached its all-time record high yesterday at 112.92. The 10-year spread over German Bunds was trading around 131 basis points, up from 127 bps this morning.
Apart from Treasury auctions, the session was dull, dealers said. "There's little to comment on," one said.
The five- and 15-year bonds were sold with a sharp decline in yields to record lows in an auction.
The shorter maturity was allotted at 6.034 percent from 6.907 percent one month ago, while the 15-year bonds were allotted at 7.149 percent from 7.638 percent.
The yields later rose again. The five-year bond was trading at the close at 105.24 from 105.68 at yesterday's end. It was yielding 6.307 percent.
